# Utter

> Utter is a native macOS menu bar app for AI-powered voice input and dictation. Hold a hotkey, speak, and polished text appears at your cursor in any app. Speech recognition and LLM cleanup run on-device on Apple Silicon; remote LLM providers are optional. MIT licensed, open source.

Utter is a macOS 26+ (Tahoe) menu bar utility for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4). It captures audio with AVAudioEngine, transcribes it locally with Qwen3-ASR, Confucius4-R2T2, FireRedASR2, Mega-ASR, WhisperKit, or on-device Apple Speech, and refines the transcript with a local MLX LLM (Qwen3.5 by default; also Qwen3, Qwen2.5, Gemma 4, Gemma 3) or a remote provider (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow, Volcengine Doubao, Alibaba Bailian, MiniMax). The result is pasted at the cursor with a simulated Cmd+V, and the previous clipboard is restored; Accessibility access is used for the hotkey and for reading the selection and nearby text as context. A Voice Command mode uses ScreenCaptureKit + the Vision framework to give the LLM on-screen context for summarizing, replying, translating, or rewriting what is visible.

Three output modes: Verbatim (raw transcription, lowest latency), Smart Format (LLM cleanup with filler removal, grammar fixes, and structured formatting), and Voice Command (screen-aware AI response).

By default, audio and transcription stay on-device; no audio upload and zero required cloud calls. Remote providers are opt-in. The UI is bilingual (English and Simplified Chinese), independent of the recognition language. Additional features include translation dictation (hold fn + shift), industry vocabularies (medical, legal, finance, software), input history with stats, input memory for continuity, personal edit rules, language style presets (casual / professional / custom), and sound feedback.

Utter is a pure Swift Package (no .xcodeproj) built with Swift 6 / SwiftUI / AppKit. Source and releases are on GitHub; the landing page is at utter.idevlab.dev.
